title: yunta config layer
description:
One config layer as parsed from a single file (project/user/org), and
also the type of the merged result — merging never needs to invent
fields, only combine what layers actually set.

commands.description:
`commands:` — `{name: command}`, what this project runs for each
capability a workflow names (`run: { command: lint }`). The name
is the workflow's, the text the project's: a pack asks for "the
lint" and the project says which tool that is.

format.description:
`format:` — which project command formats which files, run on what
a session writes the moment it writes it. The first rule whose
paths match a file formats it.

pricing.description:
`pricing:` — `{model: cost_per_1k_tokens}`, an
optional currency conversion `yunta stats` and the receipt add
*alongside* their token figures, never in place of them. Absent
means everything stays in tokens — the engine has no opinion of
its own on what a token costs, and never invents one.

secrets.description:
`secrets:` — env var *names* a session may receive; values
only ever come from the process environment at spawn time, and
nothing undeclared reaches a session's env at all.

shared_dirs.description:
`shared_dirs:` — `{VARIABLE: directory}`, directories every
command and every session of a run shares: each is exported under
its variable and stays writable inside every session that may
write, so a build cache outlives the checkout each task works in.

version.description:
`version: 1` (reference config) — the layer file's own format
version. The loader refuses any value this binary doesn't speak.

AdapterId.description: An adapter id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

AdapterSettings.description:
Adapter-specific settings: a portable binary override plus the
reference config's opaque `adapter_settings` map — this is
only for what has NO portable expression; model/agent/permissions
are typed request fields precisely so this stays small. Passed
through to `SessionRequest.adapter_settings` untouched; the adapter
validates what it can in `probe()` and rejects what it doesn't know.

AgentName.description: An agent name: printable ASCII without whitespace

BaselineConfig.description:
`baseline:` — backs the `baseline_compare` check kind; the suite the engine
runs and re-runs to catch regressions ("no regressions" as a comparison
of data, never an agent's claim).

held.description:
Project commands measured beside the suite, on the same tree: each
that passes there holds every task of a loop as a guard, as the
suite does — the project's lint, for one.

CommandName.description: A command name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

CommandPermissions.description:
`permissions.commands` — patterns matched against every hook, criterion,
bash node and executor command right before it runs. Empty
`allow` = denylist mode (everything not denied runs); a non-empty
`allow` switches to a strict, opt-in allowlist.

CoverageConfig.description:
`coverage:` — backs the `coverage_gate` check kind; `cmd`'s stdout must
contain a bare percentage (`NN[.NN]%`); the last match found is taken
as the measured coverage. Not specified any more precisely than
"measured and compared by the engine" — a permissive,
documented convention rather than inventing a stricter parsing
contract with no source to check it against.

DefaultOnFailure.description:
`defaults.on_failure` values: `pause` freezes the
run resumable, `abort` closes it failed at once, and `continue` skips
the failed node's dependents and closes failed once the rest of the
graph has run — `abort` for CI, `continue` for a run that explores.

DefaultsConfig.description:
`defaults:` — what a run and its nodes fall back to. Each field
has its consumer: `isolation`, `max_parallel_nodes`,
`on_interrupt`, `runner` (a node that declares none),
`timeout_minutes` (`Budget.timeout`), `on_failure` (what a failed
node does to the run).

max_parallel_nodes.description:
How many DAG nodes with no dependency on each other the scheduler
may run at once. Absent means the schema's own default of
`1`, not "unbounded" — the same rationale applies to
`concurrency` in loops: nobody
should discover parallel token spend by reading the bill.

on_failure.description:
What a failed node without its own `on_failure:` re-route does
to the run. Absent is `pause`, the schema's own default.

on_interrupt.description:
Fallback `on_interrupt` a node without its own
override resolves to. Same default (`restart_node`) as the
schema's own, so absent here changes nothing either.

runner.description: The runner a node without `runner:` resolves through.

timeout_minutes.description:
Per-session budget of time the host is awake (`Budget.timeout`),
in minutes, the scale of a whole session. A suspended host spends
none of it, and the run's log
records the suspension.

DiskShare.description:
An amount of a disk: bytes — `80G`, `500M`, `1.5T`, in decimal units —
or a share of the whole file system, `20%`.

Effort.description:
How long the model reasons before it answers. The four levels every
adapter's CLI accepts, each handed to it under the CLI's own name for
them; a level one CLI has and another lacks is no level here.

ExecutorKind.description:
What an executor is: a `binary`, written in any language, that speaks
JSON over its stdin and stdout. An enum with one variant rather than a
bare string, so a second kind lands with every match on it checked and
nothing else is silently accepted. Not WASM: it would sandbox an
executor at the price of a toolchain and of the languages one can be
written in, while whether a pack's executors run at all is already
`permissions.packs.executors`'s to decide.

ExecutorName.description: An executor name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

ExecutorRegistration.description:
One `skills.executors:` entry — `name` is what a `kind: executor`
node's own `executor:` field references.

ForgeConfig.description:
`forge:` — the team's forge, so `check` can tell a
`kind: gate` with `external:` apart from one with nowhere to
actually publish. GitHub only in v1, same "closed enum over an open
abstraction" stance `ForgeKind` takes on the workflow side — a
second forge is a new field here, not a schema break. `token_env`
names an env var, never carries the token itself (same
convention as `McpServerConfig::auth_env`); its absence at *runtime*
(not at `check` time — see [`GitHubForgeConfig`]) is exactly what
makes a machine with no credentials at all work:
degrade to console, don't refuse to exist.

FormatRule.description:
One rule of `format:`: the files a project command formats the moment a
session writes one of them.

paths.description: The files it formats, as scope globs.

run.description:
The project command that formats them, handed every path as an
argument.

remote.description:
The git remote a run pushes its branch to for a pull request;
`origin` when absent.

token_env.description:
The environment variable holding the token; its value never
enters the config.

GitHubRepo.description: A GitHub repository: `owner/name`, each one path segment

Isolation.description:
Whether a unit of work gets a working tree of its own, or works in
the one it was handed.

`worktree` (the default) gives it a checkout of its own, so runs work
beside each other and beside the person; `none` works directly in the
checkout it was given — legitimate for watching an agent edit live, for
CI already inside an ephemeral container, or for a tree too costly to
set up twice. A first-level run under `none` starts only from a clean
checkout, since the diff its scope is audited by could not tell the
agent's change from the person's, and holds that checkout's lock, so
no second run works there at once; its manifest records the isolation
it ran with.

One word for every level, run and `kind: workflow` node alike:
`none` is true wherever it is written, while a word naming a parent
would not be — a first-level run has no parent unit, it has a
person's checkout. `container` is not a value at all; it is not
designed. (A node that wants a tree of its own declares `scope:`,
which is what asks for one.)

LimitsConfig.description:
`limits:` — declared budgets and guards. Every field is
optional: an absent limit means "no cap", never a hidden default —
except where a limit has a default of its own
([`ConfigLayer::resolved_max_loop_iterations`](super::ConfigLayer::resolved_max_loop_iterations),
[`ConfigLayer::resolved_inline_context_bytes`](super::ConfigLayer::resolved_inline_context_bytes)),
which lives in its `resolved_*` method and nowhere else. Budgets are
advisory ceilings the engine enforces by escalation/diagnostic, never OS
enforcement.

A limit is an integer: `2000000`, or `2_000_000` with its digits
grouped, which reads as the same number — never as a string that
leaves a run without its limit.

inline_context_bytes.description:
Context sources at or under this size are inlined into the
prompt; larger ones are referenced by path.

max_artifact_bytes.description:
Guard against runaway artifacts at close: an artifact over
this size fails the node with a diagnostic.

max_concurrent_runs.description:
Best-effort cap on simultaneously non-terminal runs, checked at
run creation — a soft budget, not a safety limit (two concurrent
`yunta run` invocations can both pass the check).

max_expansion_files.description:
How many files a `rules`-mode scope expansion may touch before it
is denied as no longer "a small, adjacent set" — absent means the
reference default.

max_loop_iterations.description:
Ceiling on loop-node iterations — the only net under a tasks document
whose state oscillates forever.

max_tokens_per_run.description:
Run-wide token budget: exceeded → escalation
(`continue`/`abort`), or `run_paused { reason: budget }` with no
surface to ask.

McpServerConfig.description:
One server in `mcp_servers:` — a streamable-HTTP endpoint plus the
*name* of an env var carrying the bearer token, never the token
itself (secrets are
env var names in config, values only ever come from the process
environment at resolve time).

ModelName.description: A model name: printable ASCII without whitespace

NetworkPermissions.description:
`permissions.network` — whether the commands an agent's session runs
may reach the network when its node says nothing: the session's CLI
keeps it in its own sandbox. For any other command it is declarative;
an executor that wants to enforce it does so on its own.

OnInterrupt.description:
A node's crash-recovery policy — the full triple of options.

`restart_node` runs the node again from its start, as a new attempt:
the context it is handed is rebuilt from the run's data, so the attempt
can always begin, but its effect has to be safe to repeat.
`fail_if_uncertain` is for an effect that is not — a notification with
no key to dedupe on, a charge: a resume that finds the node running with
no terminal pauses for a person instead of guessing how it ended.

oneOf.description:
Continue the same agent conversation — the
`session_id` the log recorded (`agent_session_opened`) is
handed back to the adapter's `resume`. Only `kind: prompt` opens
a node-scoped session, so `check` refuses the explicit
declaration anywhere else; an adapter without the
`resume_session` capability — or a crash before any session
opened — degrades to `restart_node` with an explicit
`capability_degraded` event, never silently. As a *config default*
(`defaults.on_interrupt`) it applies where a session exists;
kinds without one (bash/check/…, and a loop's per-task sessions)
restart, which is the only meaning the policy can have there.

PackExecutorPolicy.description:
`allow | prompt | deny`, strictly ordered: `Deny` is the narrowest,
`Allow` the loosest — the ceiling merge keeps the strictest across
layers. `prompt` asks for confirmation at `yunta pack add`,
never mid-run: runs are headless, humans interact through gates only.

PackPermissions.description:
`permissions.packs` — governance over pack contents. Parsed and
merged here; enforced by `pack add` and `pack update`, which read the
merged value and name the layer that declared it when they refuse.

Two settings and no matrix: which publishers may be installed, and
whether a pack's executable code may run. Trusting one publisher's
executors and not another's is the allow-list with `executors:
prompt`, which asks case by case.

PathPermissions.description:
`permissions.paths` — what no node and no task of any run may write:
the project's CI, the configuration of its own checks, whatever the
team decides no agent touches. A ceiling like the rest: every layer's
denies stand, and none is ever granted back.

PathsConfig.description:
`paths:` — where a run's state lives: its run directory and its
worktree.

What a team shares is versioned in its repository, under `.yunta/`:
config, workflows, skills, agents, knowledge and packs. A run's state
belongs to whoever runs it: by default under the user state root
(`~/.yunta`, or `$YUNTA_HOME`), outside every repository, where an
agent's git commands in its checkout never reach it. `YUNTA_HOME` is an
environment override applied when resolving the merged config, not a
field of it, and a run freezes the roots it resolved
([`crate::FrozenPaths`]), so a later change to either never loses it.

PermissionsConfig.description:
`permissions:` — ONE model of ceilings, not
loose mechanisms: each level may only narrow the one above, never
loosen it. Unlike every other config group (repo > user > org), the
org layer rules here and lower layers only restrict further — without
that inversion, governance is theater: any repo could undo it.

This is governance, not a sandbox: an agent
with write access can route around a textual pattern by writing a
script and running it. The model stops the accident and the careless
pack, and leaves an auditable trail of the deliberate attempt — real
isolation belongs to the execution environment, never to Yunta.

PoolConfig.description:
`storage.pool` — both optional: what is not said falls back to what
the disk and the builds the pool measured say.

budget.description: What the builds of the project's checkouts may take together.

keep_free.description: What of the disk the pool always leaves free.

PricingEntry.description:
One `pricing:` entry (reference shape): a struct rather than a
bare number so a later per-direction price is a field addition, not
a schema break.

ProjectConfig.description:
`project:` — backs the `{{project.*}}` template namespace, the
reference config's own three fields. `base_branch` is also the branch
a `pull_request` node opens its pull request into.

Publisher.description: A publisher: one path segment: printable ASCII without whitespace, `/` or `\`, and not `.` or `..`

PublisherPermissions.description:
`permissions.packs.publishers` — `allow` empty means every publisher
is accepted.

RunnerCandidate.description:
One candidate of a runner in `runners:`: the adapter, the model it asks
that adapter's CLI for, and optionally an agent and an effort.

Three words, three things. An adapter is the integration with one agent
CLI (`claude-code`, `codex`, `mock`); a runner is the binding a node asks
for by name — the role a workflow needs, `runner: planner`, which the
project's config fills with the CLIs it has; an agent is a set of
instructions the run owns, added to the CLI's own.

agent.description:
The agent this candidate's sessions work under; a node's own
`agent:` wins over it, so the candidates of one runner may each
pair their adapter with an agent of its own.

effort.description:
How long the model reasons, unless the node says otherwise; absent
leaves it to the CLI.

RunnerName.description: A runner name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

ScopeCeiling.description:
The most permissive `scope_expansion.mode` a permissions layer allows a
node to declare: a node may declare any mode at least as strict.

ScopeExpansionMode.description:
How a loop node treats an agent's request to widen its scope.
Default `Deny`: a node that omits `scope_expansion:` entirely gets
the same behavior as one that declares it with no `mode:` — no
expansions, every request becomes a finding without interrupting.

ScopeExpansionPermissions.description:
`permissions.scope_expansion`: the layered ceiling
over how a loop node may let its tasks grow past declared scope.
`max_mode` is the most *permissive* node-level `scope_expansion.mode`
the layer allows (`rules < ask < deny` in severity) — the same
only-narrowing model every other `permissions` group follows:
merge keeps the strictest declared ceiling, a lower layer softening
it is a reported conflict, and a node declaring a mode over the
merged ceiling fails `check`.

ScopeGlob.description: a scope glob: a path pattern where `*` stays within one directory and `**` recurses

SkillName.description: A skill name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

SkillsConfig.description:
`skills:` — the executors a `kind: executor` node runs, by the name its
`executor:` gives; where the skills a node names are found; and the
skills every session mounts.

always.description:
Skill names mounted on every session, before any node's own
list.

paths.description:
Directories skill names resolve against, in order — the repo's
first. Absent means the convention default, `.yunta/skills`
(where `yunta init` installs the mechanism skill).

StorageConfig.description: `storage:` — SQLite is the only storage engine.

pool.description: What the project's checkouts may keep of the disk.
